ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: cloth put by for mending
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Someone who mends the colony's clothes wants cloth, wool or hide in the stores before the cold months wear everything thin.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: Keep at least {TARGET} cloth, wool, hide or any other textile in storage or in the home area. Grow cotton, shear the flock, tan hides, or buy from traders.

wants.reason: {PAWN_nameDef} mends the colony's clothes, and there's hardly any cloth, wool or hide left to patch them with.

plain.li: Half the colony's elbows are out of their sleeves, and I've nothing left to patch them with.
Could we put some cloth by? Winter's hard on clothes, and I can't mend with thread alone.
[winter] Every coat I mend tears somewhere else the next week. I need cloth, and plenty of it.
[tribal] We need hides put by, and good ones. The cold eats through a worn wrap in days.
[medieval] A bolt of wool in the stores would see us through the winter's mending.
[spacer] Even synthread wears through. I need something to patch it with.

warm.li: I like seeing everyone warm and whole. I just need the cloth to do it.

blunt.li: No cloth, no mending. Get some in.

cheerful.li: Give me a pile of cloth and I'll have everyone looking smart by spring.

gloomy.li: We'll all be in rags by midwinter, the way things are going.

cold.li: Mending is cheaper than making new. It still needs material.

plain.li: A proper pile of cloth to work with. Nobody's elbows are going to freeze this winter.
I've patched three coats today and there's plenty left.

warm.li: Thank you. I'll keep everyone warm with it.

cheerful.li: So much cloth. I'm going to patch everything in sight.

cold.li: The stores will cover the winter's mending.

plain.li: I'll patch with what I've got, which is mostly other patches.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: steel put by
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A builder or a crafter wants a pile of steel in the stores, so the next job or repair doesn't wait on it.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: Keep at least {TARGET} steel in storage or in the home area. Mine it, smelt down scrap, or buy it from traders.

wants.reason: {PAWN_nameDef} builds and mends with steel, and the colony's pile of it is nearly gone.

plain.li: The steel pile is down to a few bars. The next thing that breaks will just stay broken.
Could we put some steel by? I keep starting jobs I can't finish.
[tribal] The sky-metal we found is nearly used up. Our knives and arrowheads need more of it.
[medieval] A smith without iron is just someone standing by a fire. We need steel in the stores.
[industrial] Everything we build needs steel, and we're nearly out.

warm.li: I'd hate to have to tell someone their door can't be fixed for want of a few bars.

blunt.li: We're out of steel. Fix that.

cheerful.li: A nice fat pile of steel, that's all I want. Well, for now.

gloomy.li: When the next raid smashes the gate, we'll have nothing to mend it with.

cold.li: Steel is the bottleneck on half the colony's work. A reserve would remove it.

plain.li: A proper pile of steel. I can finish what I start now.
I stacked it myself. It's a good-looking pile.

warm.li: Now nobody has to wait on a repair. Thank you.

cheerful.li: Look at it all. I'm going to build something wonderful.

cold.li: The reserve should cover the next few jobs.

plain.li: We'll make do with scraps, then.

blunt.li: No steel. No repairs. Don't blame me.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: spare parts for the machines
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Someone who keeps the colony's machines running wants a few components in the stores for when one breaks down.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: Keep at least {TARGET} components in storage or in the home area. Make them at a fabrication bench, salvage them, or buy them from traders.

wants.reason: {PAWN_nameDef} keeps the colony's machines running, and the last spare parts are nearly gone.

plain.li: The next machine that breaks down will stay broken. We're out of spare parts.
Could we keep a few components by? Something always breaks at the worst time.
[night] The generator coughed twice tonight. If it goes, I've nothing to fix it with.
[winter] If the heaters break down this winter, we'll need parts the same day, not next month.
[spacer] Half our systems run on parts we can't spare. I'd sleep better with a few in the stores.

warm.li: I don't want anyone to go cold because a heater broke and I couldn't fix it.

blunt.li: Machines break. We need parts. Six, at least.

cheerful.li: A little box of spare parts would make me the happiest mechanic alive.

gloomy.li: Everything breaks down eventually. I'd rather not be standing there empty-handed when it does.

cold.li: A broken machine without a spare costs days. A handful of components costs very little.

plain.li: A box of spare parts on the shelf. Let something break; I'm ready.
I counted them twice. Enough for the next few breakdowns.

warm.li: Now nobody goes without light or heat for want of a part. Thank you.

cheerful.li: Spare parts. I could kiss every one of them.

cold.li: The reserve covers the likely failures.

plain.li: I'll keep my fingers crossed and the machines running as long as I can.

gloomy.li: When it breaks, it stays broken. Remember I said so.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: milk for the little one
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A parent with a baby wants milk or baby food in the stores, so the little one never goes hungry.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: Keep at least {TARGET} milk or baby food in storage or in the home area. Milk the animals, cook baby food, or buy milk from traders.

wants.reason: {PAWN_nameDef} has a little one to feed, and the milk in the stores won't last the week.

plain.li: There's hardly any milk left for the baby. Could we put some by?
The little one is always hungry. I'd sleep better if there were milk in the stores.
[night] I was up three times with the baby last night, and the milk jug is nearly empty.
[tribal] The little one needs milk, and our goats can't keep up on their own.
[winter] Winter's coming and there's no milk put by. A baby can't wait for spring.

warm.li: I just want to know there's enough for the little one, whatever happens.

blunt.li: The baby needs milk. We're nearly out.

cheerful.li: The little one drinks like a calf. We'll need a lot more milk.

gloomy.li: If the milk runs out, I don't know what we'll do.

cold.li: An infant needs a steady supply. The stores should hold a few days of it.

plain.li: Milk in the stores. The little one slept right through for once, and so did I.
I don't have to count the jugs any more. Thank you.

warm.li: The baby's fed, and I can breathe. Thank you, all of you.

cheerful.li: Full jugs and a fat, happy baby.

cold.li: The supply is secure for now.

plain.li: We'll manage somehow. We have to.

gloomy.li: I'll go hungry before the baby does.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: {THING} for the stores
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Someone tired of stepping over the colony's things wants proper shelves in the stores.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: The colony has {TARGET} shelves, or more.

wants.reason: {PAWN_nameDef} keeps stepping over the colony's things where they lie on the storeroom floor.

plain.li: Everything we own is in a heap on the storeroom floor. Could we build {THING} or two?
I spent an hour looking for one thing today. It was under everything else.
[rain] The damp gets into everything that sits on the floor. Shelves would keep it off.
[tribal] Even a rack of poles would keep our things off the wet ground.

warm.li: Shelves would save everyone a lot of bending and searching. Me included.

blunt.li: The stores are a mess. Build shelves.

cheerful.li: Imagine finding things the first time you look. Shelves, please.

gloomy.li: One day someone will trip over that pile and break their neck.

cold.li: Shelving holds more in less space and keeps it in order.

plain.li: Everything off the floor and in its place. I found what I wanted on the first try today.
Shelves at last. The storeroom looks like somebody cares about it.

warm.li: Thank you. Everyone's going to have an easier time of it.

cheerful.li: I've sorted everything by color. Don't touch anything.

cold.li: The stores are in order now.

plain.li: Back to digging through the pile, then.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: the trees by the walls felled
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Grown trees stand right against the colony's walls, and someone worries the next storm will bring one down on a roof. They want them felled.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: None of the {TARGET} grown trees against the walls still stands. Promised, they're marked for cutting, and the colony's cutters fell them.

plain.li: There are trees growing right against our walls. One good storm and one of them is coming through a roof.
Could we fell the trees by the walls? I lie awake listening to them creak.
[rain] The ground's soft and the trees by the walls are leaning. I don't like it.
[tribal] A tree that leans on your lodge will one day lie on it. Better we bring it down first.
[spacer] Our walls weren't built to take a falling tree. Those trees should come down.

warm.li: I don't want anyone hurt in their bed because a tree came down. Let's fell them while it's calm.

blunt.li: Trees by the walls. Cut them down.

cheerful.li: Free firewood, and a roof that stays a roof. It's a good trade.

gloomy.li: It's only a matter of time before one of them falls on someone.

cold.li: A falling tree costs a wall and maybe a life. Felling it costs an afternoon.

plain.li: The trees are down and stacked as logs. I'll sleep through the next storm.
Nothing leaning on the walls now but the wind.

warm.li: Thank you. It's one less thing to fear on a windy night.

cheerful.li: Logs for the fire and nothing over our heads but the roof.

cold.li: The risk is gone, and the wood is useful.

plain.li: The trees stay. I'll keep listening to them creak.

gloomy.li: When one comes down on a roof, remember I asked.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: the snow cleared from the doors
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Deep snow lies on the ways by the colony's doors, and someone wades through it every morning. They want it cleared.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: Nine in ten of the {TARGET} snowed-in cells by the doors are clear. Promised, they're marked for snow clearing, and the colony's cleaners shovel them.

plain.li: The snow by the doors is up to my knees. Could we clear a way out?
I waded out to the fields this morning and came back soaked to the thigh. Let's clear the ways by the doors.
[morning] It took me half the morning just to get out of the door.
[old] My knees can't take wading through that drift every morning.
[tribal] A path stamped through the snow is easier than a drift. Let's clear the ways to the lodges.

warm.li: A cleared path to the door would make everyone's mornings easier.

cheerful.li: I'll race anyone to the end of the path once it's cleared.

gloomy.li: Someone's going to slip in that drift and not get up.

cold.li: Deep snow slows every trip out of the door. Clearing it pays for itself in a day.

plain.li: Clear ways by the doors. I walked out this morning without filling my boots.
Someone shoveled the drifts away. My knees thank them.

warm.li: Thank you. Everyone's mornings are easier now.

cheerful.li: I can see the ground. Well, a path of it.

plain.li: Wading again, then.

gloomy.li: The snow will melt eventually. I'll be cold until then.
